Article Title: 'Bones will mend but shattered dreams?' Rahul Gandhi meets Bihar students shot at during protest
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi with injured student protesters

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday shared a video of his interaction with three students who were injured during police action amid recent student protests in Bihar.The three were part of a group of students from Bihar who met the Lok Sabha leader of opposition at his Delhi residence on September 3. In a social media post, Gandhi said the three students had been “shot at”, referring to a protest in Siwan, Bihar, on July 25.“Think about it: what crime had these children committed that they were shot? They had asked the government for just three things — education, employment, and accountability,” the Raebareli MP wrote on X.The leg bone of one of the students, he added, was shattered after he was hit by a bullet fired from an AK-47.“Along with it, his dream of joining the Army and serving the country was shattered too. Bullets tore through the shoulders of two other students,” Rahul Gandhi wrote.“They were not criminals. They were children from poor families who had gone out to study carrying the dreams of their families — some wanted a good job, while others wanted to change the circumstances of their homes,” he added.The Congress leader further remarked that while their physical wounds would heal, there is no answer to how the psychological trauma they had suffered could be treated."Mr prime minister, Mr chief minister — their broken bones will heal. Can you give them back their broken dreams?" Rahul Gandhi said, questioning Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary.Several parts of Bihar witnessed student protests, some of which turned violent, on July 25 as part of a broader agitation by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Delhi. The CJP was leading protests demanding the resignation of then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak issue, along with reforms in the education system.The CJP, which had been protesting at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar since June 21, called off its agitation on July 25, shortly after Pradhan resigned. Union minister Pralhad Joshi has since been given additional charge of the Education ministry.The Bihar government has told the Supreme Court that a police constable fired four rounds from an AK-47 into the air after being trapped in a crowd, while maintaining that no protester was injured in the firing. The constable has since been suspended.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi shared a video of his interaction with three students injured during police action amid recent student protests in Bihar. The three were part of a group of students from Bihar who met the Lok Sabha leader of opposition at his Delhi residence on September 3. Gandhi said the three students had been “shot at”, referring to a protest in Siwan, Bihar, on July 25.

Article Title: Congress replaces Bhupesh Baghel with Sachin Pilot as Punjab general secretary
Article Text:
Sachin Pilot replaces Bhupesh Baghel as Congress gereral secretary for Punjab

NEW DELHI: The Congress on Saturday appointed Sachin Pilot as the party’s general secretary in-charge of Punjab, replacing Bhupesh Baghel, news agency PTI reported.The appointment comes as Congress prepares to strengthen its organisation and political strategy in the state ahead of the Punjab assembly elections.Congress had appointed former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel as an AICC general secretary and made him the party’s Punjab in-charge in 2025.A prominent OBC leader, Baghel was credited with helping revive the Congress in Chhattisgarh and led the party to a landslide victory in the 2018 assembly elections.He served as chief minister from 2018 to 2023, with his tenure focusing on pro-farmer policies and rural development.Congress, however, lost the 2023 Chhattisgarh polls to the BJP, with Vishnu Deo Sai subsequently becoming chief minister.
Article Summary: Congress appoints Sachin Pilot as party's general secretary in-charge of Punjab. Pilot replaces Bhupesh Baghel as Congress gereral secretary for Punjab. appointment comes as Congress prepares to strengthen its organisation and political strategy in the state ahead of the Punjab assembly elections.

Article Title: Gardener Dead in Maidan Garhi Farmhouse
Article Text: New Delhi: A 28-year-old gardener was found dead inside a room at a farmhouse in south Delhi ’s Maidan Garhi area, police said.Police said they received information around 4.12pm on Sept 2 that a man was lying face down inside a room at the farmhouse. When they arrived at the spot, they found the man dead. There were serious injury marks around his neck.The body was taken into custody and sent for postmortem.Preliminary investigation revealed that the deceased, identified as Ishtiyaq, had an altercation with another gardener working nearby. During the argument, the accused allegedly assaulted Ishtiyaq and fled, causing his death, police said.A case has been registered, and efforts are under way to trace the accused.
Article Summary: A 28-year-old gardener was found dead inside a room at a farmhouse in south Delhi ’s Maidan Garhi area, police said. Police received information around 4.12pm on Sept 2 that a man was lying face down in a room. There were serious injury marks around his neck.

Article Title: MCOCA action against two accused from ‘Gold Hunters Gang’ in Kolhapur
Article Text:
Kolhapur

:





Special inspector general of police, Ranjan Kumar Sharma, has approved action under the Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) against two alleged members of the “Gold Hunters Gang,” arrested in a gold chain theft case in Kolhapur.The accused are alleged gang leader, Vaibhav Narayan Adole (26), a Hinjewadi resident and native of Yerla in Amravati district, and Karan Gorakh Jagadhane (19), a resident of Vidhate Vasti in Aundh and native of Pimpalwadi in Paithan.Police said 28 serious cases, including forcible theft, housebreaking and vehicle theft, were registered against the duo across Maharashtra, including six in Kolhapur.They allegedly engaged an elderly woman in conversation before fleeing, on the pretext of asking for an address before snatching a 20gm mangalsutra from her neck, near Ambai Tank in Kolhapur.A parallel investigation by the local crime branch led to their arrest at Shirwal in Satara district. Police said 26 cases involving gold chains stolen from elderly women were registered across Maharashtra.The investigation found that the duo had allegedly committed offences in Kolhapur, Sangli, Satara, Sawantwadi, Kankavli, Kudal, Pune, Wardha, Buldhana, Beed, Akola, Amravati and Yavatmal.Superintendent of police, Nilotpal directed Juna Rajwada police station inspector, Kiran Londhe to prepare the MCOCA proposal. Havaldar Ranjit Desai and colleagues prepared it.Additional superintendent of police Annasaheb Jadhav, deputy superintendent Priya Patil, local crime branch inspector Sushant Chavan and assistant faujdar Sachin Patil scrutinised the proposal before sending it for approval.
Article Summary: Alleged gang leader Vaibhav Narayan Adole (26) and Karan Gorakh Jagadhane (19) arrested in Kolhapur. Police said 28 serious cases, including forcible theft, housebreaking and vehicle theft, were registered against the duo across Maharashtra.

Article Title: FIR lodged after 3,400 SIR forms found in Navi Mumbai shop; 5 BLOs suspended
Article Text:
An FIR was registered against Suraj Patil for illegally possessing voter enumeration forms





NAVI MUMBAI: The police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting special intensive revision (SIR) voter enumeration forms for “personal use” and for breaking the maintenance of secrecy of voting under Section 314 of the BNS and Section 128 of the Representation of People Act.Section 314 of the BNS deals with dishonestly converting a movable property for own use, for which the punishment is at least two years imprisonment.The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar. He alerted the police.The accused (Patil) had decamped from the Kharghar police station, leading to high drama throughout the night.Authorities seized 3,404 SIR forms, including 11 blank ones, of 11 polling stations from the photocopier’s shop next to the Ramsheth Thakur Public School in Sector 19, Kharghar, by Shiv Sena (UBT) nodal chief Balesh Bhojane.Five booth-level officers (BLOs) served with show-cause notices were suspended by the Panvel City Municipal Corporation (PCMC) chief Mangesh Chitale.They include three data entry operators working as booth-level officers from a private company, Saunik Integrated & Security Pvt Ltd, Bhayandar, engaged by the PCMC.Their names are Sulochana Mane, Prashant Mhatre and Rahul Bhagat.The Shiv Sena (UBT) had earlier warned the Panvel sub-divisional officer through a letter about various lapses in the electoral process.A two-member inquiry committee comprising a Panvel deputy municipal commissioner, Nanasaheb Kamathe, and an assistant electoral registration officer, has been formed to conduct a comprehensive probe.Bhojane said, “MLAs Jitendra Awhad and Rohit Pawar have tweeted the video regarding the original SIR forms at the Kharghar shop. We demand action against the Panvel SDO as he did not take preventive measures despite our complaint about forms filed at the BJP offices. The FIR was filed only after more than hundreds of our workers assembled at the police station.”After learning about the incident, Raigad district communication head of Shiv Sena (UBT) Prasad Bhoir lodged a complaint with the electoral registration officer.“Yesterday evening, the election registration office (ERO) received information that a person is xeroxing enumeration forms at a Xerox centre at Kharghar sector 19. Immediately, the assistant election registration officer visited the site and found that one Suraj Patil was holding around 3,400 enumeration forms and xeroxing it illegally,” Raigad district collector Kishan Javale said.
Article Summary: Police have registered an FIR against Suraj Patil, a nodal BJP youth wing committee member, for illegally possessing and converting voter enumeration forms. The matter came to light on Thursday, after an advocate working for the Shiv Sena (UBT) noticed hundreds of original SIR forms lying at a photocopier’s shop in Kharghar.

Article Title: Alandi boarding school teacher acquitted of charges linked to 11-yr-old student’s death in classroom assault
Article Text:
Pune





: A sessions court at Khed has acquitted a teacher of a spiritual boarding school at Alandi of the charges of attempted murder and culpable homicide not amounting to murder in connection with the death of an 11-year-old Std V student allegedly due to medical complications arising out of an assault in the classroom.The alleged assault took place 10 to 11 days prior to the registration of the FIR by the Alandi Devachi police station on Feb 20, 2020, based on a complaint from the student’s mother. The victim died on March 27, 2020, while under treatment at a private hospital. The accused, who was arrested on the day of the registration of the FIR, was released on bail on Jan 11, 2023.Additional sessions judge A S Sayyad, in a judgment pronounced on Feb 16, found that the prosecution evidence was “brittle and scanty which is insufficient to establish the charge against the accused beyond all reasonable doubt. The prosecution therefore failed to establish the charge against the accused.”The court questioned the basis for the application of the culpable homicide charge while observing that in a case of assault by a teacher on a student with a small stick, the medical certificate of the doctor who first treated the deceased was absent in respect of the nature of injury being simple or grievous.Moreover, the seven fellow students, who were presented as witnesses in front of whom the alleged assault took place, did not support the prosecution case during the trial.The court also cited gaps in the evidence of some of the witnesses.“This appears a failure of the investigating officer while carrying out the proper investigation in the case. It would not be outplace to state that the investigation regarding the crime is not properly conducted and it seems not free from doubt,” the court said.
Article Summary: A sessions court at Khed has acquitted a teacher of the charges of attempted murder and culpable homicide not amounting to murder. The alleged assault took place 10 to 11 days prior to the registration of the FIR by the Alandi Devachi police station on Feb 20, 2020. The victim died on March 27, 2020, while under treatment at a private hospital. The accused was released on bail on Jan 11, 2023.

Article Title: Amadea partner withdraws anticipatory bail plea in Mundhwa land case
Article Text:
Pune:

pursis





Amadea Enterprises LLP partner Digvijay Patil has withdrawn his anticipatory bail application from a city court in the case linked to the Mundhwa govt land parcel deal registered by the Khadak police and being investigated by the Economic Offences Wing.Patil cited the reason of need to amend his pleadings and grounds for the anticipatory bail relief in the wake of the chargesheet filed by the police during the pendency of his application.The case relates to two illegal orders passed by suspended Pune city tehsildar Suryakant Yewale, granting ownership rights of govt lands in Mundhwa and Bopodi in favour of private parties, registered with the Khadak police. In one of these orders, Yewale had written to the Botanical Survey of India, which possesses the land on lease till 2038, to vacate the same in favour of Amadea Enterprises LLP in which former deputy chief minister late Ajit Pawar’s son, Parth, is another partner.Parth has not been named in the FIR. Patil has been named in the case with Sheetal Tejwani, the power of attorney holder for the 272 Watandars (original holders of the Mahar Watan land before the Mahar Watan system was abolished), Yewale and six others linked to the Bopodi govt land parcel related order. The Enforcement Offences Wing (EOW) filed a 1,886-page chargesheet against Tejwani on Jan 27.Patil’s lawyer S S Kulkarni filed a(information to court) before the court of additional sessions judge BV Wagh on Feb 18 stating that, during the pendency of the present (anticipatory bail) application, the Investigating agency filed the chargesheet against other co-accused in the present matter.“In view of the filing of the chargesheet, it became necessary for the applicant (Digvija Patil) to reconsider, and amend the pleadings and grounds in light of the material contained in the chargesheet and accompanying documents,” he stated.“Therefore, the applicant seeks to withdraw the said bail application with liberty to file a fresh application, if necessary, after examining the chargesheet and taking appropriate grounds,” the application stated. The court allowed the plea on these grounds by stating that the application was disposed of as withdrawn.
Article Summary: Amadea Enterprises LLP partner Digvijay Patil has withdrawn his anticipatory bail application. The case relates to two illegal orders passed by suspended Pune city tehsildar Suryakant Yewale, granting ownership rights of govt lands in Mundhwa and Bopodi in favour of private parties.

Article Title: Man gets 7-year rigorous imprisonment for sexually harassing minor girl in Nashik’s Panchavati
Article Text:
Nashik

:





A special Pocso court in Nashik on Friday sentenced a 44-year-old man to seven years of rigorous imprisonment for sexually harassing a minor girl after luring her with snacks in the Panchavati area in 2020.District and sessions judge R N Pandhare convicted the accused under Section 10 of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (Pocso) Act, 2012. The court also imposed a fine of Rs 3,000, with an additional three months of simple imprisonment in case of default.The court further directed the convict to pay Rs 50,000 as compensation to the girl within a month. Failure to do so will attract an additional one-year simple imprisonment.According to the prosecution, the incident occurred on Nov 9, 2020, between 4pm and 5pm at a slum locality in Panchavati. The accused allegedly took advantage of the absence of the girl’s family members, lured the girl with biscuits and sexually harassed her. He was also accused of engaging in obscene behaviour.Based on a complaint lodged by the girl’s family, Panchavati police registered an offence under sections 354 and 354(A) of the Indian Penal Code, along with relevant provisions of the Pocso Act.The investigation was conducted by then sub-inspector Dhanashree Patil of Panchavati police station. She collected crucial circumstantial evidence and subsequently filed a chargesheet before the court.Additional public prosecutors Bhanupriya Pethkar and R P Gavit represented the state and presented witness testimonies and evidence before the court, leading to the conviction. Following the verdict, Nashik police commissioner Sandeep Karnik and deputy commissioner of police (crime) Kirankumar Chavan lauded the efforts of the investigating officers, prosecution team and court liaison staff for securing the conviction.
Article Summary: A special Pocso court in Nashik on Friday sentenced a 44-year-old man to seven years of rigorous imprisonment for sexually harassing a minor girl. The court also imposed a fine of Rs 3,000, with an additional three months of simple imprisonment in case of default. The incident occurred on Nov 9, 2020, between 4pm and 5pm at a slum locality in Panchavati.

Article Title: 11-year-old Mumbai boy drowns in Godavari river
Article Text:
(Representative image) An 11-year-old boy from Mumbai drowned in the Godavari River on Saturday morning





NASHIK: An 11-year-old boy from Mumbai's Ghatkopar drowned in the Godavari River at Gandhi Talav in Nashik's Panchavati area on Saturday morning.The boy was identified as Gopal Umesh Gupta.According to Panchavati police, Gopal was among a 40-member group from Uttar Pradesh who are currently living in Ghatkopar. The group had reached Panchavati on Saturday morning to visit temples in the area.The incident took place when four boys from the group entered the river while the women went to change their clothes. Local youths who dive into the river to collect coins thrown by devotees spotted the boys struggling in the water.The youths, along with lifeguards nearby, rescued three of the boys. A few minutes later, the group noticed that Gopal was missing. Local divers went back into the river and found him.Gopal was taken to the district civil hospital, where doctors declared him dead on arrival.Panchavati police have registered a case of accidental death and are investigating the incident.
Article Summary: 11-year-old boy from Mumbai's Ghatkopar drowned in the Godavari River in Nashik. The boy was identified as Gopal Umesh Gupta. Police have registered a case of accidental death and are investigating the incident.

Article Title: Tribal woman dies after family planning surgery in Salem; relatives lay siege to collectorate in protest
Article Text:
Over 100 relatives and villagers laid siege to Salem district collectorate in protest

Salem:





A tribal woman died at the Attur govt Hospital on Thursday, after her health deteriorated following a sterilisation surgery at Pethanaickenpalayam primary health centre in Salem district.The deceased has been identified as M Sumathi, 23, of Soolankurichi hill village in Karumanthurai. She was referred to Attur govt hospital soon after the sterilisation procedure but died without responding to treatment. She had delivered her third child about 45 days ago.Over 100 relatives and villagers including her husband Matheawaran, 30, laid siege to Salem district collectorate in protest. They alleged that a botched surgery had caused her death and demanded justice.Police held talks with the protesters and officials assured them that a proper inquiry would be held against the doctors concerned and appropriate action taken. The protesters subsequently withdrew their protest.Attur rural police have registered a case and are investigating.
Article Summary: The deceased has been identified as M Sumathi, 23, of Soolankurichi hill village in Karumanthurai. She was referred to Attur govt hospital soon after the sterilisation procedure but died without responding to treatment.

Article Title: Not an act of political vendetta: Nirmal Kumar
Article Text:
Electricity minister C T R Nirmal Kumar on Saturday said the searches conducted by directorate of vigilance and anti-corruption (DVAC) at properties linked to former minister K N Nehru were not an act of political vendetta.





Madurai: Electricity minister C T R Nirmal Kumar on Saturday said the searches conducted by directorate of vigilance and anti-corruption (DVAC) at properties linked to former minister K N Nehru were not an act of political vendetta.Speaking to reporters in Madurai, he said no one had the authority to interfere with the DVAC’s functioning. “The searches were routine and based on the evidence. No one can interfere with the DVAC. No one knows what is happening there. The department will release details,” he said, rejecting allegations that the TVK govt’s action was politically motivated.Asked about statements by AIADMK and DMK leaders that the TVK govt would not last, Nirmal Kumar said they indicated that the two parties were together. He also said there was a possibility of the AIADMK, DMK and BJP forming an alliance for the next election.Regarding the omission of the Board of Trustees’ names from the invitation for the consecration ceremony of Sri Meenakshi Sundareswarar temple, Nirmal Kumar said, “None of us will interfere in temple affairs, particularly those concerning the HR&CE department. Even our review is limited to assessing the arrangements made for devotees. We will not repeat the mistake made by the previous govt in temple matters.”
Article Summary: Electricity minister C T R Nirmal Kumar said the searches conducted by directorate of vigilance and anti-corruption (DVAC) at properties linked to former minister K N Nehru were not an act of political vendetta. “The searches were routine and based on the evidence. No one can interfere with the DVAC,” he said.

Article Title: Plea seeks child safety committees in all TN educational institutions
Article Text:
Madras high court has sought a response from the state education department on a plea seeking a directive for the constitution of child safety committees in all govt, aided and private educational institutions in Tamil Nadu.





Madurai: Madras high court has sought a response from the state education department on a plea seeking a directive for the constitution of child safety committees in all govt, aided and private educational institutions in Tamil Nadu A division bench of Justice C V Karthikeyan and Justice R Sakthivel was hearing a public interest litigation filed by C Selvakumar of Madurai.The petitioner stated that a private higher secondary school teacher was arrested in Madurai on the charges of sexually harassing a girl student in 2025. The incident demonstrates the need to strengthen child-safety mechanisms more broadly in all govt, govt-aided and private schools and colleges in the state.He stated that an effective preventive mechanism should ensure that there is a safe and accessible method for students to complain; that parents are appropriately informed; that competent child-protection authorities — and, wherever the law mandates, police — are promptly involved; and that no such matter is suppressed or treated merely as an internal disciplinary issue where a statutory offence is alleged.He stated that such a mechanism should not replace the statutory functions of the authorities. Its purpose should be preventive, facilitating safe reporting, coordinating between competent authorities, and monitoring compliance with child-safety measures. Its composition, powers, functions and confidentiality safeguards may be determined by the govt authorities, who can also be directed to conduct periodic awareness and sensitisation programmes for students, parents, teachers, non-teaching staff and administrators.The case was adjourned for hearing on Oct 27.
Article Summary: Madras high court has sought a response from the state education department on a plea seeking a directive for the constitution of child safety committees in Tamil Nadu. A private higher secondary school teacher was arrested in Madurai on the charges of sexually harassing a girl student in 2025.

Article Title: HC seeks response on plea to install effluent treatment plants at govt hospitals
Article Text:
Madras high court sought a response from the state on a plea seeking a direction for installation of effluent treatment plants at all govt hospitals in districts falling under Madurai bench’s jurisdiction.





Madurai: Madras high court sought a response from the state on a plea seeking a direction for installation of effluent treatment plants at all govt hospitals in districts falling under Madurai bench’s jurisdiction.A division bench of Justice C V Karthikeyan and Justice R Sakthivel was hearing a public interest litigation filed by advocate R Manibharathi of Madurai.The petitioner stated that the biomedical waste such as pathological, microbiological, discarded medicines, human tissues, organs, dressings, sharps, contaminated plastics, liquid biomedical waste, blood, saliva, body fluids and other infectious materials is inherently hazardous.He stated that unless handled strictly in accordance with scientific standards prescribed under law, biomedical waste poses serious risks of spreading diseases, contaminating groundwater, damaging the ecosystem and endangering lives. The improper disposal of such sewage from the hospitals also contributes to antimicrobial resistance, occupational exposure to infectious pathogens and long-term environmental degradation.He stated that the issue assumes greater significance because the govt hospitals cater predominantly to economically weaker sections of society. Every patient entering a govt hospital is entitled to receive medical treatment in a safe and hygienic environment. Equally, sanitation workers and healthcare professionals are entitled to protection from avoidable occupational exposure arising out of improper waste management practices.The petitioner stated that Govt Rajaji Hospital (GRH) in Madurai generates enormous quantities of biomedical waste every day and it is not treated properly as the hospital’s sewage treatment plant is not working properly, resulting in sewage being discharged directly into Vaigai river.Hence, the petitioner moved court seeking a direction to the authorities to install effluent treatment plants with adequate capacity in all govt health facilities in the districts under Madurai bench’s jurisdiction. The petitioner also sought a direction to the authorities to conduct periodic inspections to verify the proper functioning of effluent treatment plants in all the govt hospitals and sought the strict implementation of the guidelines for green and climate-resilient healthcare facilities. The case was posted for hearing on Oct 8.
Article Summary: Madras high court sought a response from the state on a plea seeking a direction for installation of effluent treatment plants. A division bench of Justice C V Karthikeyan and Justice R Sakthivel was hearing a public interest litigation filed by advocate R Manibharathi of Madurai.

Article Title: NDA leader will be PM in 2029, EPS will be back as CM: AIADMK
Article Text:
NDA leader will be PM in 2029, EPS will be back as CM: AIADMK





Madurai: Even as allies TVK and Congress are projecting their respective leaders as prime ministerial candidates in 2029, former AIADMK ministers have said neither chief minister C Joseph Vijay nor Rahul Gandhi will become the PM.Instead, an NDA leader endorsed by AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami would be the PM, AIADMK leaders said on Friday. They also said that simultaneous elections would be conducted for the state assembly along with parliamentary elections and that EPS would come to power in Tamil Nadu.“Edappadi K Palaniswami’s five decades in public life would give him a decisive role within NDA. Whoever EPS endorses as the NDA’s prime ministerial candidate will receive the people’s mandate in the 2029 Lok Sabha election,” said former minister R B Udhayakumar. Udhayakumar on Friday said the debate over projecting Vijay or Rahul Gandhi as the prime ministerial candidate had exposed divisions between TVK and Congress.He said the Tamil Nadu assembly election would be held simultaneously under the proposed “One Nation, One Election” system. “EPS would then return as chief minister,’’ he said.Another former minister, Sellur K Raju, said the Vijay govt was unstable and could collapse before completing its term.“Your film (Jananayagan) did not run, and your govt will not run either,” he said.Raju said the govt remained dependent on its allies. “The patient is still in the ICU. Nobody knows when its oxygen level will fall or when life support will be withdrawn,” he said stating that Congress or the communist parties could withdraw support at any time.Rejecting comparisons between Vijay and AIADMK founder M G Ramachandran, Raju said, “Can you match even one of the thousand things MGR did?”
Article Summary: Former AIADMK ministers say neither C Joseph Vijay nor Rahul Gandhi will become the PM. Instead, an NDA leader endorsed by Edappadi K Palaniswami would be the PM, they said. simultaneous elections would be conducted for the state assembly along with parliamentary elections and that EPS would come to power in Tamil Nadu.

Article Title: Salem corporation council meeting disrupted over mayor’s demand for removal of deputy mayor chair from dais
Article Text: COIMBATORE: Tension flared at the Salem corporation council meeting on Friday when mayor A Ramachandran, who belongs to DMK, refused to conduct the proceedings, insisting that the chair of deputy mayor Saradha Devi, who belongs to Congress, be moved from the dais.The council meeting of Salem corporation, scheduled to begin at 11am, started 20 minutes late after the mayor entered the hall. Instead of taking his designated seat, the mayor sat among the councillors and declared that he would not preside over the session. He stated that during the previous council meeting, he had ordered to remove the deputy mayor’s seat from near the mayor’s chair. However, he alleged that the Salem corporation commissioner overruled his directive and insisted on retaining deputy mayor’s chair next to that of the mayor. “I will not conduct this meeting where I am not given the authority,” Ramachandran said.DMK councillors protested demanding the removal of the deputy mayor’s chair from the dais. When corporation staffers attempted to remove the chair, Saradha Devi launched a sit-in protest in the council hall. She accused the mayor of showing gender bias and disrespect.She said, “The mayor does not give me the respect I deserve because I am a woman.My chair has been right next to the mayor’s for the last four years; why should it be removed now? I respect this council, and I will not allow my seat to be moved.”Following the uproar, a closed-door reconciliation meeting was convened between the corporation commissioner, mayor, deputy mayor, and DMK councillors. Emerging from the discussions, Saradha Devi alleged, “They spoke about shifting my seat from the dais and asked whether I wanted the ‘chair’ or a ‘share.’ I made it clear that I only want my chair.”The deadlock remained unresolved. Upon returning to the council hall, mayor Ramachandran announced that all resolutions were postponed due to the disruption. He left the hall after that. However, Saradha Devi continued her protest.Tension between Congress and DMK councillors started after the national party left the DMK alliance to join the TVK govt in the state in May.
Article Summary: DMK councillors protested demanding the removal of the deputy mayor’s chair from the dais. When corporation staffers attempted to remove the chair, Saradha Devi launched a sit-in protest in the council hall. She accused the mayor of showing gender bias and disrespect.

Article Title: Police intercepts car in Angamaly, seize 12kg ganja
Article Text:
Kochi:





Ernakulam Rural police seized 12kg of cannabis from a car near Angamaly on Saturday.Charles Dennis, 29, and Praveen Das, 28, of Punnapra, Alappuzha, were arrested by a joint team of rural Dansaf unit and Angamaly Police.Acting on intelligence received by district police chief K S Sudarshan, officers intercepted the accused near Angamaly TB Junction. The ganja was found carefully packed in bags concealed in the car’s boot. Investigators say the consignment was headed for Alappuzha. The investigation team included narcotic cell DSP C Binu Kumar, Aluva DSP Baiju Paulose, and Angamaly SHO PM Razik.Earlier this week, on Tuesday, Kochi city police conducted raids at two separate locations within city limits, seizing more than 26kg of ganja in total.In Eloor, a West Bengal native was arrested with 14.13kg of ganja within Eloor police station limits. The accused, who worked collecting scrap for a shop in the Muttar area, was caught transporting the cannabis in his scrap-collecting three-wheeler at Manjummel. On Aug 31, a check conducted near Ernakulam South railway station within Kadavanthra police station limits led to the arrest of two Odisha natives with 12.15kg of cannabis in their possession.With more than 38kg of cannabis seized in less than a week, police have intensified their probe into the supply network bringing narcotics into the district from other states. Police have appealed to the public to report any information related to the smuggling and distribution of narcotics.
Article Summary: Charles Dennis, 29, and Praveen Das, 28, of Punnapra, Alappuzha, were arrested by a joint team of rural Dansaf unit and Angamaly Police. The ganja was found carefully packed in bags concealed in the car’s boot. Earlier this week, on Tuesday, Kochi city police conducted raids at two separate locations within city limits.

Article Title: College student in Ettumanoor Police’s custody for morphing classmates photos
Article Text:
Kottayam

:





Ettumanoor Police have taken a youth into custody for allegedly hacking into a classmate’s Instagram account and morphing her photographs, along with those of other classmates, into obscene images.According to the complaint, the accused illegally accessed the complainant’s Instagram account and used photographs taken during college events to create fake obscene images, using his mobile phone and laptop. The fabricated images were allegedly stored in a hidden folder on his phone, the police said.The complainant and her friends came across the images on Sept 3, following which she approached the police alleging defamation and mental distress, said the cops.A case has been registered at Ettumanoor police station. The accused has been taken into custody, and his mobile phone and laptop have been sent for detailed examination, the police said.
Article Summary: Ettumanoor Police have taken a youth into custody for allegedly hacking into a classmate’s Instagram account and morphing her photographs, along with those of other classmates, into obscene images. The fabricated images were allegedly stored in a hidden folder on his phone.
